subject: GK
text: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi launch the historic Quit India Movement?
explanation: The Quit India Movement, also known as the August Movement, was launched on August 8, 1942, during World War II, demanding an end to British rule.

subject: GK
text: Which country is globally known as the 'Land of the Rising Sun'?
explanation: Japan is referred to as the Land of the Rising Sun because from China's perspective, the sun rises in the direction of Japan.

subject: GK
text: Who was the first Indian (and Asian) to receive a Nobel Prize?
explanation: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his collection of poems titled 'Gitanjali'.

subject: GK
text: What is the national animal of India?
explanation: The Royal Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris) was declared the national animal of India in April 1973 with the launch of Project Tiger.

subject: GK
text: Which gas do humans inhale for respiration and cellular energy production?
explanation: Oxygen ($O_2$) is inhaled by humans and used in cellular respiration to break down glucose and release energy.

subject: GK
text: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of India?
explanation: Indira Gandhi served as the first and, to date, only female Prime Minister of India from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 to 1984.

subject: GK
text: Which amendment act to the Indian Constitution granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions?
explanation: The 73rd Amendment Act of 1992 added Part IX and the 11th Schedule to the Constitution, establishing a three-tier Panchayati Raj system.

subject: GK
text: Where is the headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO) located?
explanation: The WTO, which replaced GATT in 1995 to regulate international trade, is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

subject: GK
text: Which is the deepest ocean trench in the world, located in the Western Pacific?
explanation: The Mariana Trench contains the deepest known point on Earth, the Challenger Deep, measuring nearly 11,000 meters.

subject: GK
text: What is the term of office for an elected member of the Rajya Sabha (Upper House of Indian Parliament)?
explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body; its members are elected for a term of 6 years, with one-third retiring every 2 years.

subject: GK
text: Which Indian city, capital of Rajasthan, is popularly known as the 'Pink City'?
explanation: Jaipur was painted pink in 1876 under the rule of Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh to welcome the Prince of Wales, hence the nickname.

subject: GK
text: Where is the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) located?
explanation: BARC, India's premier nuclear research facility, is situated in Trombay, Mumbai, Maharashtra.

subject: GK
text: Which ocean is the largest by surface area and volume?
explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean, covering more than the entire landmass of Earth combined.

subject: GK
text: Under which article of the Indian Constitution can the Governor of a state promulgate ordinances when the legislature is not in session?
explanation: Article 213 empowers the Governor to promulgate ordinances, having the same force as an act of the state legislature.

subject: GK
text: Who was the President of India when the National Emergency was declared in June 1975?
explanation: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed signed the emergency proclamation on the advice of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, which lasted until 1977.

subject: GK
text: In which year was the historic Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed in New Delhi?
explanation: The pact was signed on March 5, 1931, between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin, leading to the suspension of Civil Disobedience.

subject: GK
text: What is the term of office for an elected judge of the International Court of Justice (ICJ)?
explanation: The ICJ consists of 15 judges elected for 9-year terms by the UN General Assembly and Security Council.

subject: GK
text: Which Indian state is the largest producer of Gold, accounting for nearly 99% of India's gold production?
explanation: Karnataka is the leading producer of gold, primarily from the Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) and Hutti Gold Mines.

subject: GK
text: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by all United Nations Member States in 2015?
explanation: The UN Agenda 2030 established 17 interconnected SDGs (such as No Poverty, Zero Hunger) to achieve a sustainable future.

subject: GK
text: In which Indian city is the main campus of the National Chemical Laboratory (NCL) situated?
explanation: NCL, a constituent laboratory of CSIR, is located in Pune, Maharashtra, established in 1950.

subject: GK
text: What is the localized, hot, dry summer wind that blows during afternoons in the northern plains of India called?
explanation: The 'Loo' is a strong, dusty, hot summer wind that blows in the Indo-Gangetic plains, causing heat strokes.

subject: GK
text: Which British committee was appointed in 1927 to suggest constitutional reforms in India, but boycotted by Indians for lacking any Indian member?
explanation: The Simon Commission, headed by Sir John Simon, was boycotted under the slogan 'Simon Go Back' because it had no Indian representation.

subject: GK
text: What was the primary, controversial provision of the Rowlatt Act passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in 1919?
explanation: The Rowlatt Act authorized the British government to arrest and detain any person without warrant or trial for up to two years.

options.text: Imposition of high taxes on local salt production
Imprisonment of political suspects without trial and warrant for up to two years
Complete ban on vernacular press publications
Prohibition of trade with foreign nations in cotton

subject: GK
text: In monetary economics, what does Gresham's Law state?
explanation: Gresham's Law states that 'bad money drives out good money' from circulation if they have equal legal tender value but different commodity values.

options.text: Rising prices cause inflation to outpace supply
Bad money drives out good money from circulation
Higher interest rates lead to increased savings

subject: GK
text: Which Indian environmental activist is famously celebrated as the 'Waterman of India' for reviving traditional water harvesting structures (johads) in Rajasthan?
explanation: Rajendra Singh founded Tarun Bharat Sangh and won the Magsaysay Award in 2001 for his work in rain water harvesting and managing water tables.
